episode_title: 038 - The Sound of Collaboration w/ Wesley Slover

real_qa.q: What is Sanctus Audio and why did Wesley Slover rebrand from Sonos Sanctus?
real_qa.r: Wesley Slover runs Sanctus Audio, a small sound and music design studio focused on music composition and creative direction. The company was previously named Sonos Sanctus, but Slover changed it because clients were confusing it with Sonos the speaker company, and the original name was difficult to remember and communicate effectively as a brand.

real_qa.q: How did Wesley Slover transition from pursuing video game audio to motion design?
real_qa.r: After audio engineering school around 2005, Slover struggled to break into video game audio despite internship experience. He worked on various projects including friend's films, church services, and live sound. His career breakthrough came when motion designer Jordan Scott introduced him to creating sound effects for a baking blog video, which revealed to him that motion graphics was a thriving industry outside of Pixar and Saturday morning cartoons.
real_qa.requete: Wesley Slover motion design career entry

real_qa.q: What types of industries and projects does Sanctus Audio work on besides motion design?
real_qa.r: Sanctus Audio has worked on indie games preparing for Steam's Next Fest, UX sound design for Loom and Discord product features, industrial 3D printer audio design, live-action film, and radio broadcast audio. Slover describes their approach as evaluating any project with sound or music needs and determining how audio can help achieve the project's goals.
real_qa.requete: Sanctus Audio projects Discord Loom Steam

real_qa.q: What is the typical production timeline and workflow for Sanctus Audio's sound and music design process?
real_qa.r: Sanctus Audio's role is typically faster than animation, with involvement throughout the entire project but coming in and out as needed. They contribute to pre-production budgeting and planning, create a sound style frame early to establish direction, then coordinate in parallel with animation to avoid extending the schedule. The company emphasizes flexibility because project schedules frequently shift, especially affecting their end-of-project work window.

real_qa.q: What is The Collab Collection podcast by Wesley Slover about?
real_qa.r: The Collab Collection is Wesley Slover's podcast exploring collaboration in creative work. Slover created it after realizing there are abundant technical skill tutorials online but few resources about working well with other people. The podcast features interviews with creative professionals and other collaborators, including stories from motion designers, mural painters, and artists, sharing insights about how collaboration works across different creative fields and contexts.

guest.bio_context: Wesley Slover grew up as a musician playing trumpet and guitar, eventually pursuing audio engineering at a tech school around 2005. He discovered his career focus in motion design after collaborating with motion designer Jordan Scott on a baking blog video project, realizing there was a thriving community of animators outside mainstream studios. He now runs Sanctus Audio, a sound and music design studio that works across motion design, video games, UX design, and live-action film.

real_quote: Everything is built on collaboration. Everything is built on how well can we collaborate with the clients that we're working with.
